title: The Greatest Showman
tagline: Roll up. Roll up. Dinner is served.
about: A dreamer from nothing builds a dazzling circus show in 1800s New York.
cue: Serve the snacks when the troupe sings This Is Me.
faces: Men suffer more from imagining too little than too much.

    Snack BarGeneral Tom Thumb's roasted peanutsPeanuts roasted in the shell with flaky salt and smoked paprika, in paper conesHow to make it400g peanuts in the shell1 tsp flaky salt1 tsp smoked paprikaSpread the peanuts on a tray.Roast at 180°C.Toss hot with flaky salt and smoked paprika.Roll paper into cones and fill them up.The Greatest Show caramel popcornPopcorn coated in brown sugar caramel and baked until crispHow to make it120g popcorn kernels2 tbsp vegetable oil150g brown sugar80g butter3 tbsp golden syrup1/2 tsp bicarbonate of soda1 pinch of saltPop the kernels in the oil and spread on two lined trays.Boil the sugar, butter and golden syrup, then stir in the bicarbonate of soda and salt.Pour over the popcorn and toss.Bake at 120°C, stirring every 15 minutes.Hot CounterJenny Lind opening night roastSirloin roast, potatoes, Yorkshire puddings and red wine gravyHow to make it1.5kg beef sirloin1kg potatoes, peeled and halved3 tbsp olive oil3 eggs150g plain flour300ml milk200ml red winesalt and pepper, to tasteHeat the oven to 200°C. Season the beef and roast until 52°C inside.Rest the beef under foil.Roast the potatoes in oil.Whisk the eggs, flour and milk and bake in hot oiled tins at 220°C.Reduce the red wine with the pan juices for gravy.Swedish Nightingale meatballsJenny Lind, the Swedish singer on her American tourHow to make itNot on tonight's cookPork and beef meatballs with allspice, browned in butter and simmered in a creamy brown gravy, with buttery mash, lingonberry jam and quick pickled cucumber.Mix 400g beef mince, 300g pork mince, 1 grated onion, 50g breadcrumbs soaked in 80ml milk, 1 egg, half a teaspoon of allspice and salt.Roll 28 balls and brown in butter.Stir 2 tbsp flour into the pan, whisk in 400ml beef stock, 100ml cream and 1 tsp soy, add the meatballs and simmer 10 minutes.Toss sliced cucumber in vinegar, sugar and dill.Serve with mash and lingonberry jam.Candy CaseRingmaster's red velvet cakePhillip takes over as ringmaster. Red velvet, cream cheese frosting.How to make it125g butter, softened250g caster sugar2 eggs250g self-raising flour2 tbsp cocoa250ml buttermilk1 tbsp red food colouring250g cream cheese250g icing sugar1 tbsp gold sprinklesHeat the oven to 175°C and line two tins.Beat the butter and sugar, add the eggs, then fold in the flour, cocoa, buttermilk and colouring.Bake in two tins.Cool, then beat the cream cheese and icing sugar.Layer and cover the cake and add gold sprinkles.Sideshow red toffee applesBarnum rides an elephant to the ballet recital. Toffee apples, salted peanuts.How to make itNot on tonight's cookCrisp green apples on sticks dipped in a glassy red toffee, half rolled in crushed salted peanuts before it sets.Wash and dry 8 small green apples and push a stick into each.Boil 400g caster sugar, 150ml water, 2 tbsp golden syrup and 1 tsp vinegar to 150°C without stirring, then add red food colouring.Tip the pan and dip each apple, twisting, then roll the bottom in 60g crushed salted peanuts and set on baking paper for 15 minutes.Fountain and BarBarnum's champagne cocktailsSugar cube, bitters, cognac and champagne, sparkling apple juice for non-drinkersHow to make it4 sugar cubes8 dashes of aromatic bitters60ml cognac1 bottle of cold champagne1 lemon, peel onlyPut a sugar cube in each of 4 coupes and soak with bitters.Add cognac to each.Slowly top with cold champagne.Twist lemon peel over and drop it in. Use sparkling apple juice and a dash of bitters for the younger crowd.
